events.description: El trombón gana protagonismo en la música clásica y contemporánea: Beethoven, Berlioz y Britten lo utilizan de manera expresiva en sus obras.

events.title: Integración Folclórica
events.description: En Colombia, aunque el trombón no es tradicionalmente protagonista en los ritmos patrimoniales, ha comenzado a tener mayor presencia en agrupaciones modernas, bandas sinfónicas y fusiones contemporáneas.

cumbia.title: Cumbia
cumbia.description: Ritmo emblemático de la región atlántica, que nació fusionando elementos africanos, indígenas y españoles. El trombón aporta profundidad y carácter a esta expresión musical.

currulao.title: Currulao

pasillo.title: Pasillo y Bambuco
pasillo.description: Géneros representativos de la región andina colombiana donde el trombón ha encontrado un espacio especial para expresar la melancolía y alegría de nuestra montaña.

joropo.title: Joropo
joropo.description: Música llanera que con la incorporación del trombón ha ganado nuevas dimensiones sonoras, manteniendo la esencia del trabajo y la vida en los llanos orientales.

items.conclusion: Thus demonstrating the versatility and expressive capacity of the instrument in autochthonous musical contexts.

items.description: Through a historical and territorial journey, we aim to account for the current state of Colombian folklore as well as the evolution that led it to mix with practices as complex as orchestral ones, with the trombone as the main element. From this, the composition of the suite is proposed as a contribution to the repertoire of Colombian rhythms representative of each region of the country.

specificObjectives.subtitle: Specific Objectives
items: Identify the type of rhythm according to Colombian regions.
Know the contribution of the trombone in each of them (rhythms).
Understand why the trombone has little prominence within the identified and chosen rhythms.
Propose a composition that contributes to each of the rhythms to be addressed, with the trombone as the clear protagonist.

heroSection.title: History of the Trombone in Colombia
heroSection.description: A journey from Europe to the heart of Colombian folklore

heroSection.title: Cumbia
heroSection.description: Atlantic Coast - The rhythm that conquered Colombia's heart

historicalDescription.title: History and Cultural Context
historicalDescription.content: Cumbia, whose name comes from the word "cumbancha", is perhaps the most representative and important rhythm of the Atlantic region. Born from the fusion between African cadence, indigenous monotonous sounds, and the festive character of the coast, cumbia is a national symbol recognized even outside Colombia.
historicalDescription.quote: Cumbia with trombone represents the natural evolution of our traditions, where each instrument contributes its voice to the ancestral choir of the Atlantic Coast.

mainTypes.title: Main Types
items: Modern cumbia: in addition to traditional instruments, it includes singing (telling stories of coastal experiences)
Classical cumbia: characterized by the absence of voices and the prominence of instruments, especially the guacharaca

tromboneRole.title: Trombone's Role
paragraphs: The trombone found its place in cumbia during the 20th century, when pelayera bands began incorporating brass wind instruments to enrich the traditional sound. Its deep and expressive timbre perfectly complements ancestral rhythmic patterns, providing harmonic and melodic depth to the ensemble.

In contemporary cumbia interpretation, the trombone plays both melodic and harmonic roles, dialoguing with the gaita, accordion, and percussion to create unique sound textures that maintain the folkloric essence while embracing instrumental modernity.

heroSection.title: Currulao
heroSection.description: Pacific Coast - African ancestrality in modern sound

historicalDescription.title: History and Cultural Context
paragraphs: The origin of the word currulao is closely related to cunuano, which refers to the type of drum called cununo, an important instrument when talking about rhythms from the Pacific region.

It is a flagship rhythm within the Afro-Colombian population, also influenced by enslaved black communities in Latin America, who brought with them traditions of santería and religious rites, which is why those who interpret it as part of their culture attribute ancestral properties to it, it's like a kind of ritual.
It is accompanied by a traditional dance that bears the same name (currulao).
historicalDescription.quote: Currulao with trombone is the meeting of two sound worlds: African ancestrality and instrumental modernity, creating new forms of cultural expression.

traditionalInstrumentation.title: Traditional Instrumentation

tromboneContribution.title: Trombone's Contribution
tromboneContribution.content: Currulao and cumbia, typical of Colombian coastal areas, were characterized by their speed and interesting combination of percussion with wind instruments. Although in this case the trombone is not the protagonist either, it is an important contribution for its subsequent inclusion within the rhythms addressed, since its union with our tradition occurs or opens through areas that develop along the sea.

heroSection.title: Pasillo and Bambuco
heroSection.description: Andean Region - The melancholy and joy of our mountains

historicalDescription.title: History and Cultural Context

pasillo.title: Pasillo
paragraphs: Pasillo is one of the most recent national rhythms, as it emerged during the independence era, in contrast to other rhythms that developed during the colonial period. Its musical foundation comes from the Austrian waltz, mixed with creole dances from the interior of Colombia.

Initially it was performed in salons, mainly with piano, but later became popular in more humble sectors by including instruments such as guitar, tiple, and bandola. This transition gave pasillo a more festive and dynamic character, making it a fast and technical rhythm that represents challenges for both musicians and dancers.

bambuco.title: Bambuco
paragraphs: Bambuco is considered the most representative rhythm of the Colombian Andean region. Unlike pasillo, its performance is usually handled by small groups (2 or 3 musicians) and is accompanied by instruments such as guitar, tiple, and even flute in some versions.

This deeply peasant rhythm is the result of a rich racial mix, being one of the emblems of national folklore, although not so well known outside the country. Sanjuanero, for example, is a derivation of bambuco. Throughout history, bambuco has had contact with rhythms such as the Cuban habanera, which evidences the dialogue between cultures in its evolution.

historicalDescription.quote: In pasillo and bambuco, the trombone sings the stories of our people, their joys and nostalgias, their celebrations and remembrances.

pasillo.title: Trombone in Pasillo
items: Historical participation: It was not part of the original groups. Pasillo was mainly played with piano, guitar, tiple, and bandola.
Current protagonism: In this thesis we present the movement "Confusion (Pasillo)", in which we propose the trombone as the central instrument.
Technical challenge: A lyrical and explosive melodic line is sought that allows the trombone to stand out without overshadowing the symphonic band.
Reason for inclusion: Vindicate the trombone as part of the national repertoire through a reinterpretation of the festive pasillo in symphonic format.

bambuco.title: Trombone in Bambuco
items: Aesthetic challenge: Integrating it involves balancing the trombone's power with bambuco's melodic essence.
Symphonic adaptation: The symphonic band allows instrumental expansion where the trombone can play a leading role.
Cultural justification: Internationalization movements and contact with music from the Caribbean, Mexico, and South America opened the way for wind instruments.
Compositional proposal: The trombone is proposed as a lyrical instrument that dialogues with the orchestra, inspired by the concerto grosso.
Expressive impact: The trombone can contribute emotion, dynamism, and depth to the Colombian Andean repertoire, without sacrificing identity.

heroSection.title: Joropo
heroSection.description: Orinoquía - The spirit of the plains in new sound dimensions

historicalDescription.title: History and Cultural Context
paragraphs: This musical type developed during the colonial period with Hispanic creole traditions and slight African influences, it has a fast rhythm also with a bit of waltz mixture, its singing is called copla, its main instruments are the harp, cuatro, and a type of maraca called capacho.
In this type of music, musical confrontations are held where singing predominates, these competitions are called contrapunteo. In the Orinoquía, the word joropo means dance and celebration.

Joropo dance is vigorous and demanding. It is usually performed in pairs, with short and fast steps that imitate the trot of horses, thus symbolizing the bond between the peasant and nature. In many versions, dancers also perform energetic stomping that reinforces the festive and tribal character of the rhythm.
historicalDescription.quote: Joropo with trombone is like the wind that crosses the plains: it maintains its ancestral force but embraces new sound horizons.

musicalCharacteristics.title: Musical Characteristics
items: Fast and syncopated rhythm, with strong presence of 3/4 and 6/8 in musical meter.
Improvised copla as a form of lyrical expression.
Vocal contrapunteo between performers, which demonstrates ingenuity and mastery of oral tradition.
Stomping dance with great rhythmic force, performed in pairs.
Festive, cheerful, and combative character, associated with rural life and community celebrations.
Narrative content in the lyrics, which speak of landscape, cattle, love, and regional pride.

instrumentation.title: Instrumentation
items: Llanera harp or bandola
Llanero cuatro
Maracas (of the capacho type)

variants.title: Variants
items: Llanero Joropo
Central Joropo

tromboneContribution.title: Trombone's Contribution
items: Historical absence: In its peasant roots, the trombone was not present in traditional joropo. Instrumentation was limited to harp, cuatro, and maracas.
Technical limitations: The original format did not offer spaces or arrangements for brass wind instruments due to its acoustic and intimate nature.
Contemporary potential: Currently, the trombone can be incorporated into symphonic arrangements and modern llanera bands to enrich joropo's sound.
Expressive contribution: Its ability to produce lyrical and explosive lines makes it an excellent vehicle for melodic drama within joropo-based works.

Symphonic proposal: The inclusion of the trombone in compositions is proposed as part of the reinterpretation of this rhythm in orchestral key, maintaining the festive spirit but expanding instrumental color.
Instrumental dialogue: The trombone can establish counterpoints with the harp and cuatro, imitating vocal contrapunteo, which allows enriching timbral games in a symphonic band.
